ref-hs-601-22087.name: Boeing / Hughes 601 (HS-601)
ref-hs-601-22087.description: Two stacked equipment modules, opposed solar wings and outboard communications reflectors. Antenna sizes and placement represent a typical 601 payload.

ref-hs-601hp-24916.name: Boeing / Hughes 601HP (HS-601HP)
ref-hs-601hp-24916.description: High-power 601 with extended solar wings, a separate communications module and side-mounted reflectors. Payload fittings vary by mission.

boeing-601-msat.name: Boeing / Hughes 601 · MSAT
boeing-601-msat.description: The MSAT spacecraft carry two 5.7 × 5.3 m springback L-band reflectors on a Hughes 601 bus.
boeing-601-msat.dimensionNote: Body and array dimensions are representative estimates. The two reflector apertures use the published dimensions.

ref-bss-702-41724.name: Boeing BSS-702 · reference bus
ref-bss-702-41724.description: Representative 702 body and deployed wings. External payload details for these catalog entries are uncertain.

ref-bss-702hp-26608.name: Boeing BSS-702HP
ref-bss-702hp-26608.description: High-power bus with paired solar wings, folding thermal radiators and side-mounted communications antennas. SES-9 is the visual reference for this family.

ref-hs-702-26038.name: Boeing / Hughes 702 · concentrator wings
ref-hs-702-26038.description: Early 702 with reflective troughs flanking both solar wings. Galaxy XI is the visual reference.

boeing-702hp-inmarsat5.name: Boeing BSS-702HP · Inmarsat-5
boeing-702hp-inmarsat5.description: Five panels per solar wing, deployed thermal radiators and a Ka-band payload. The six offset reflectors follow the published Inmarsat-5 F4 configuration.

ref-bss-702mp-38098.name: Boeing BSS-702MP
ref-bss-702mp-38098.description: Medium-power 702 with paired solar wings and perimeter reflectors. The four-panel Intelsat 21 is the representative configuration.

boeing-702mp-three-panel.name: Boeing BSS-702MP · Intelsat 22
boeing-702mp-three-panel.description: Intelsat 22 uses three solar panels on each wing of the 702MP.

ref-bss-702mp-56370.name: Boeing BSS-702MP+ · ViaSat-3
ref-bss-702mp-56370.description: Nominal ViaSat-3 design with eight panels on each cross-shaped solar wing and one offset mesh reflector at the end of a long boom.
ref-bss-702mp-56370.dimensionNote: Solar span is the published 144 ft, rounded to 43.9 m. The reflector diameter and position are estimates from operator renderings. Individual deployment anomalies are outside this model.

ref-bss-702sp-40424.name: Boeing BSS-702SP
ref-bss-702sp-40424.description: Compact all-electric bus with a light radiator face, opposed solar wings and side-mounted reflectors. SES-15 is the representative exterior.

boeing-702sp-ses-cband.name: Boeing BSS-702SP · SES-20 / SES-21
boeing-702sp-ses-cband.description: Twin C-band satellites share a compact 702SP bus with a pair of outboard reflector assemblies. The shared exterior follows SES's deployed illustration.

ref-hs-gem-26578.name: Boeing GEO-Mobile · Thuraya
ref-hs-gem-26578.description: GEO-Mobile platform with a deployable 12.25 m L-band mesh reflector on an offset support.
ref-hs-gem-26578.dimensionNote: The 12.25 m aperture is published. The central bus and support are estimated independently of the deployed reflector.

boeing-thuraya-concentrators.name: Boeing GEO-Mobile · Thuraya-1
boeing-thuraya-concentrators.description: Early GEO-Mobile bus with a 12.25 m L-band mesh antenna and reflector troughs alongside its solar panels.
boeing-thuraya-concentrators.dimensionNote: Catalog array span, published antenna aperture and estimated central bus and support.

boeing-geomobile-22m.name: Boeing GEO-Mobile · 22 m reflector
boeing-geomobile-22m.description: A 22 m mesh antenna dominates the SkyTerra-1 and Morelos-3 exteriors. A smaller solid antenna sits opposite the mesh assembly.
boeing-geomobile-22m.dimensionNote: Published 22 m aperture and representative catalog wingspan. Secondary antenna, bus depth and support geometry are approximate.

ref-eurostar-3000-28187.name: Airbus Eurostar E3000
ref-eurostar-3000-28187.description: Gold-insulated communications module with two outboard reflectors and articulated solar wings. SES-11 is the representative exterior.

ref-eurostar-neo-54048.name: Airbus Eurostar Neo
ref-eurostar-neo-54048.description: Modular Eurostar Neo with outboard antennas and widened middle sections on its solar wings. The Airbus product illustration is the representative configuration.

ref-eurostar-neo-56757.name: Airbus Eurostar Neo · BADR-8
ref-eurostar-neo-56757.description: ArabSat Eurostar Neo platform, represented by the shared Airbus product-line exterior.

ref-spacebus-neo200-49332.name: Thales Alenia Space Spacebus NEO200
ref-spacebus-neo200-49332.description: Box-shaped service module, separate gold-insulated payload, extended solar yokes and outboard reflectors. SES-17 is the visual reference.

ref-dfh-4-31395.name: CAST Dongfanghong DFH-4
ref-dfh-4-31395.description: Three-axis communications platform with a service module, a payload module and opposed solar wings. Antenna layout varies with the payload.
ref-dfh-4-31395.dimensionNote: CGWIC gives the bus envelope as 2.36 × 2.10 × 3.60 m. The 30 m solar span is representative catalog data.

goes-i.name: GOES I–M
goes-i.description: Two-panel solar wing opposite a 17.7 m solar-sail boom, with a separate 3 m magnetometer boom. The 26.9 m tip-to-tip dimension includes the sail and the array.
goes-i.dimensionNote: Published sail reach and total length. The wing and body occupy the remaining 9.2 m.

goes-n.name: GOES N–P
goes-n.description: Boeing 601-based weather bus with a single-panel wing, separate imager and sounder housings, and an 8.5 m magnetometer boom.
goes-n.dimensionNote: NASA bus length and width and NOAA magnetometer boom length. Array reach is approximate.

goes-r.name: GOES-R series
goes-r.description: Five-panel solar wing with instruments on the inboard Sun Pointing Platform, a separate antenna wing and an 8.5 m magnetometer boom.

himawari-8-9.name: Himawari 8 and 9
himawari-8-9.description: AHI on a raised imager bench, an offset Ka-band dish and a single two-panel solar wing on a triangulated yoke.
himawari-8-9.dimensionNote: JMA gives a 2.2 × 2.1 × 2.9 m bus and a deployed envelope of approximately 5.1 × 8.0 × 5.3 m.

mtg-i.name: Meteosat Third Generation Imager
mtg-i.description: Opposed single-panel solar wings and a separate instrument module carrying the Flexible Combined Imager and the four Lightning Imager optical heads.

mtg-s.name: Meteosat Third Generation Sounder
mtg-s.description: Opposed single-panel solar wings and a separate instrument module carrying the infrared sounder and the Sentinel-4 spectrometer.

tdrs-1.name: TDRS generation 1 (A–G)
tdrs-1.description: Two 4.9 m gimbaled single-access reflectors, a separate space-to-ground link dish and a multiple-access antenna deck.
tdrs-1.dimensionNote: Nominal deployed aperture diameter and catalog solar-array span. The bus envelope, feed supports and array drive are approximate.

tdrs-2.name: TDRS generation 2 (H–J)
tdrs-2.description: Two 4.6 m gimbaled single-access reflectors, a separate space-to-ground link dish and a multiple-access antenna deck.
tdrs-2.dimensionNote: Nominal deployed aperture diameter and catalog solar-array span. The bus envelope, feed supports and array drive are approximate.

tdrs-3.name: TDRS generation 3 (K–M)
tdrs-3.description: Two 4.6 m gimbaled single-access reflectors, a separate space-to-ground link dish and a multiple-access antenna deck.
tdrs-3.dimensionNote: Nominal deployed aperture diameter and catalog solar-array span. The bus envelope, feed supports and array drive are approximate.

ref-ekran-9503.name: Ekran
ref-ekran-9503.description: Cylindrical broadcast satellite with two pairs of solar paddles and a four-section, 96-element helical antenna array.

ref-gorizont-11158.name: Gorizont
ref-gorizont-11158.description: Stepped cylindrical service module, broad paired solar wings and an axial communications reflector with an exposed feed. Fittings follow the deployed drawing in figure 41.

ref-ats-f-7318.name: NASA Applications Technology Satellite 6 (ATS-6)
ref-ats-f-7318.description: An open mesh parasol separates the Earth-viewing module and its prime-focus feed from the two curved solar paddles.
ref-ats-f-7318.dimensionNote: NASA figure 1-3 gives the 16 m span and 8.61 m deployed height. The text gives a 9.14 m reflector. The module and truss fittings are estimated.

ref-spacebus-4000b2-33056.name: Thales Alenia Space Spacebus 4000B2
ref-spacebus-4000b2-33056.description: Koreasat-7 represents this platform with a gold communications bus, large and small side reflectors, and two solar wings on open yokes. Payload fittings vary by mission.

ref-spacebus-4000c4-33453.name: Thales Alenia Space Spacebus 4000C4
ref-spacebus-4000c4-33453.description: The SGDC launch illustration shows the long bus, four outboard reflectors and opposed solar wings. The shared model represents this communications configuration.

ref-a2100a-26495.name: Lockheed Martin A2100A
ref-a2100a-26495.description: Two offset reflectors, an equipment deck and opposed solar arrays follow the VINASAT-2 illustration. Bus dimensions and payload fittings vary across the platform.

ref-a2100axs-35755.name: Lockheed Martin A2100AXS
ref-a2100axs-35755.description: The JCSAT-13 launch illustration shows four side reflectors and a pair of five-panel wings with exposed yokes.

lm2100-jcsat17.name: Lockheed Martin LM 2100 · JCSAT-17
lm2100-jcsat17.description: Mobile communications spacecraft with an 18 m S-band mesh reflector. The nominal array and smaller payload antennas are representative.
lm2100-jcsat17.dimensionNote: The operator specifies an 18 m reflector. The catalog provides an estimated bus size and array span. Antenna offsets and supports are estimated.
